input: Reach out to three industry contacts for informational chats

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether the contacts need to be identified first or are already chosen changes whether the task starts with research or drafting outreach immediately.
The type of industry professionals targeted (e.g., peers, senior leaders, people at specific companies) shapes who to contact and how to frame the message.
Understanding the purpose behind these chats — job search, business development, learning, a career pivot — fundamentally changes the tone and agenda of the outreach.
A deadline for when all three chats should be confirmed or completed affects how urgently to follow up and how many contacts to reach out to in parallel.
The channel used for outreach (LinkedIn, email, phone, mutual intro) determines the format and length of the message and the immediate next action.
The desired tone of the message — warm and casual vs. formal and professional — changes how the outreach is written and how the ask is framed.
Knowing what a successful outcome looks like — a reply, a confirmed meeting, or a completed conversation — defines when this task is actually done.

gold.taskTitle: Reach Out to Three Industry Contacts for Chats
gold.taskDescription: Identify and contact three industry professionals to set up informal informational conversations.

questions.title: Do you have three contacts in mind, or do you need to find them?
questions.description: Determines whether the task begins with identifying/researching contacts or goes straight to writing outreach messages.

questions.title: What type of professionals are you hoping to connect with?
questions.description: Clarifies the seniority level, role type, or company profile of the target contacts to ensure outreach is aimed at the right people.

questions.title: What is the main reason you want these conversations?
questions.description: Establishes the underlying goal — job search, career pivot, business development, industry learning — which shapes the entire framing of the outreach.

questions.title: When do you need all three chats confirmed or completed by?
questions.description: Sets a deadline to determine urgency, follow-up cadence, and how many contacts to approach simultaneously.

questions.title: Which channel will you use to reach out to these contacts?
questions.description: Identifies whether outreach happens via LinkedIn, email, phone, or a mutual introduction, which dictates the format and length of the message.

questions.title: Should the tone of your message be warm and casual or more formal?
questions.description: Guides how the outreach message is written — whether it reads like a note from a peer or a structured professional request.

questions.title: What counts as done — a reply, a booked meeting, or a completed chat?
questions.description: Defines the finish line so progress can be tracked and the task can be marked complete at the right moment.
